feedback: grilled accept: the submit/cancel pairing makes the close vocabulary complete — submit finished work for the human decision (success half), cancel marks it no longer needed (the opposite). The model's only no-longer-needed terminal is the retired artifact-era superseded (derivation + leg gate still understand it; writer gone; name means version-replacement). This task makes cancelled a first-class live terminal: event + derived status (never overrides done/failed; blocked/waiting never override it — the escape for stuck blocked tasks) + closed-set parity with done/superseded so a cancelled task never blocks its leg. PLUS the dogfooding status gap: confirm-accepted-but-not-completed currently derives queued and looks re-runnable — it needs its own honest intermediate word. Decisions: any initiator cancels (append-style, RECORDED_BY, reason required); queued/active/blocked all cancellable. Recorded on 08-task-close/01.
